# 412 Maple Ridge Dr — pricing brief

Prepared 2026-08-29. This is a marketing pricing brief, **not an appraisal** and not a
valuation. Source: four closed sales pulled from the MLS on 2026-08-29, adjusted against
paired-sales rates for 37172. The title company's figures govern at closing.

## The supported range

**$504,000 to $528,000**, with the middle of the adjusted sales at $515,000.

That range is not an opinion about the house. It is where four comparable sales land once
each one is adjusted to stand in for this property, with every adjustment shown below.

## The four sales, and what each was adjusted for

| Comp | Closed | Adjusted to | Why it moved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 118 Bellwood Ct | $498,000 | $522,981 | smaller, older, and an inferior lot |
| 243 Kestrel Ln | $512,500 | $503,206 | larger with an extra bath and a newer build year |
| 87 Harlow Dr | $486,000 | $529,708 | the largest adjustment here — one fewer bedroom and materially less finished area |
| 355 Quarry Bend | $505,750 | $506,873 | the closest match on record; almost nothing to adjust |

87 Harlow Dr carries the biggest adjustment, so it carries the least weight. 355 Quarry Bend
needed almost none, which is why it anchors the middle of the range.

## The two sales that were left out

**1502 Ridgecrest Way, $561,000.** New construction backing the golf course. It is the highest
number in the neighborhood and it is the one an online estimate will find first. It is not
comparable to a 1998 interior lot, and using it would set a price this house cannot defend at
appraisal.

**9 Old Mill Rd, $402,000.** An estate sale, sold as-is, and outside the twelve-month window.
Leaving it in would drag the range down as unfairly as Ridgecrest would push it up.

Both exclusions are listed here on purpose. A comp set is only worth what its exclusions are.

## What you would net

Estimates, at three prices inside the range.

| List price | Estimated costs | Payoff | Estimated net to you |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $504,000 | $37,685 | $214,300 | $252,000 |
| $515,000 | $38,433 | $214,300 | $262,000 |
| $528,000 | $39,339 | $214,300 | $274,000 |

The spread between the bottom and the top of the range is about $22,000 in your pocket. That is
the number worth deciding against, rather than the list price on its own. [computed]

## What moves this

Condition on the day we photograph, and the buyer-side compensation you decide to offer, which
is negotiated separately and is not published on the MLS. Both change the table above. Neither
changes the comp set.
